Hi Maya — thanks for the note and for the PDF. Putting answers below and attaching our artifacts (egress-ip-rotation-plan.xlsx, flowlog-correlation-playbook.md) for your evidence pack.

Short answers up front:
- Nominal rotation window: 15 minutes for ephemeral assignments by default; configurable to a 1–60 minute window depending on tenant SLA.
- Session identifier: yes — each runtime connection includes a UUID session_id that we surface in our flow telemetry and in X-Redwood-Session headers for proxied HTTP(s) (where applicable).
- Artifacts: see attached rotation plan and our flowlog playbook. We can provide a signed PDF (SLA amendment) for audit if required.

Design notes / caveats:
- We use short-lived NAT allocations to keep per-token cost low and to enable horizontal reuse. That means a given external IP may be reused across tenants over time; rely on the session_id + flowlog correlation for post-hoc attribution, not static IP ownership.
- For long-lived connections (websockets or pinned reverse tunnels) we support an optional sticky mapping that pins egress IP for the connection's lifetime — this must be requested at provisioning time and carries an increased capacity charge.
- Connection draining: when we rotate IPs we perform a 30s drain where active TCP/WS connections are signaled; ephemeral allocations may extend beyond rotation while drain completes.

Operational deliverables we propose:
1) Signed rotation plan (attached) with rotation cadence and retention windows.
2) Flowlog correlation playbook (attached) describing how to join our session_id to VPC flow logs and our CDN logs for an audit timeline.
3) Runbook snippet for emergency freeze/rollback and an SLA amendment template (we can DocuSign).

Next steps:
- If that matches your risk posture, we can schedule a 30-minute technical review. I suggest Wed 30 Sep 10:00–10:30 PT; invite enclosed in calendar link.
- If you need per-tenant static egress addresses instead, we'll provide a reserved IP pool quote.

Thanks — Evelyn

Eve / team — a couple of operational points to add before we send to Brightline:

- Stateful firewall interaction: recommend we call out that customers must allow established TCP flows (stateful) for a 45s window to accommodate drain/FIN behavior when rotation occurs — otherwise short-lived requests may see RSTs.
- SYN retries: if perimeter does aggressive SYN drop, include guidance for increasing client-side SYN retries by 1.
- DNS caching: if Brightline uses internal DNS split-horizon that pins FQDN->IP locally, rotation will be invisible; encourage FQDN-based allowlist of our private endpoint plus a minimal IP-range fallback for emergencies.
- Audit correlation: we will add an example BigQuery query for matching VPC flow logs with our session_id; include that in the playbook.

I'll add these bullets to the playbook and push an update to the doc link.

—Laura

Maya — following up with the consolidated deliverables and next steps. See summary below; full artifacts attached and linked.

Summary for audit committee:
- Rotation cadence: default 15 minutes; negotiable 1–60 minutes per tenant.
- Attribution model: do not rely on IP owner semantics for long-term ownership. Use our session_id (present in flow telemetry and X-Redwood-Session header) + VPC flow logs to attribute sessions. We have a playbook with join queries and sample timestamps.
- Sticky sessions: available on request for long-lived connections; increases reserved capacity billing.
- Drain window: 30s drain + recommend allowing established state for 45s at perimeter.
- Evidence provided: egress-ip-rotation-plan.xlsx, flowlog-correlation-playbook.md, and draft SLA amendment (sla-exception-amendment-draft.pdf).
